theory.intro: Data collection faults during surveys, experiments, or observational studies invalidate results. Diagnosing errors like interviewer influence, missing controls, or faulty instruments allows researchers to fix the process.
facts: The **interviewer effect** occurs when participants alter answers to please an interviewer or avoid embarrassment.
Asking sensitive questions without **anonymity** leads to dishonest answers or non-participation.
**Non-response bias** occurs when many selected participants do not respond and no follow-up is done.
Experiments require a **control group** or placebo to separate the treatment effect from natural changes.
**Confounding variables** are uncontrolled external factors that influence results alongside the tested variable.
**Measurement error** arises from uncalibrated or faulty instruments producing inaccurate readings.
The **observer effect** alters participant behaviour when watched, while **recall error** distorts self-reported memories.
**Transcription errors** occur when manual mistakes are made transferring data into digital records.

foundation.question_text: A school principal stands in front of each classroom and asks students to raise their hands if they have ever cheated on an exam. Identify the data collection fault.
foundation.solution_text:
Students will not answer honestly about cheating in front of the principal due to fear of disciplinary consequences.
Interviewer effect and lack of anonymity on sensitive questions.

foundation.question_text: A scientist tests a new plant fertiliser on $20$ tomato plants in a greenhouse and observes that they grow $15\text{ cm}$ in a month. No plants are grown without the fertiliser. Identify the fault in the experimental design.
foundation.solution_text:
Without a control group of plants grown under identical conditions without fertiliser, there is no baseline to determine how much growth occurred naturally.
Lack of a control group.

foundation.question_text: A nutrition researcher asks adults to recall the exact number of grams of protein and carbohydrates they consumed on each day over the past three months. Identify the fault in this data collection method.
foundation.solution_text:
People cannot accurately remember exact food weights and nutritional quantities consumed months ago.
Recall error in self-reported data.

foundation.question_text: A study compares the effect of a new study technique by testing Group A in a quiet morning session at $21^{\circ}\text{C}$ and Group B in a noisy afternoon session at $32^{\circ}\text{C}$. Identify the experimental fault.
foundation.solution_text:
Noise and temperature differed between the groups, introducing extraneous factors that influence test performance.
Inconsistent experimental conditions and confounding variables.

foundation.question_text: A police department surveys community members about their trust in local officers by having uniformed officers conduct face-to-face door-to-door interviews. State how to fix this data collection process to obtain truthful data.
foundation.solution_text:
Uniformed officers create an interviewer effect where residents feel pressured to report high trust.
Use an anonymous, self-administered online or mail-in questionnaire with no police presence.

foundation.question_text: A workplace manager sits directly behind factory employees with a clipboard and stopwatch to record their standard daily work speed. Explain why the recorded speeds may be inaccurate.
foundation.solution_text:
Workers know they are being watched by management and temporarily increase their working speed.
Observer effect (Hawthorne effect).

foundation.question_text: A hospital surveys discharged patients by mailing $1000$ questionnaires. Only $80$ patients reply, and the hospital records their responses without following up the remaining $920$ patients. Identify the data collection fault.
foundation.solution_text:
A $92\%$ non-response rate without follow-up means the collected data reflects only patients with extreme experiences.
High non-response rate without follow-up.

development.question_text: An athletic trainer tests a new sports drink on a running squad. The trainer uses an electronic timing gate for the morning pre-test and a handheld manual stopwatch for the afternoon post-test. Identify the data collection fault and explain its impact.
development.solution_text:
Switching between automatic timing gates and manual stopwatches introduces human reaction time error.
Instrument and measurement error, producing inconsistent timing measurements.

development.question_text: A clinical trial tests a new headache medication by giving the active drug to $50$ patients and recording how many report pain relief after $1$ hour. Describe what must be added to make this a valid experimental design.
development.solution_text:
The trial lacks a control comparison to account for the placebo effect or natural recovery.
Add a control group of 50 similar patients given an identical-looking placebo (inactive pill) in a double-blind trial.

development.question_text: A research assistant manually types $5000$ handwritten numerical health surveys into a spreadsheet. Upon auditing $50$ random entries, $8$ contain transposed digits (such as typing 81 instead of 18). Identify the data collection fault.
development.solution_text:
Manual transcription of handwritten data leads to human typing mistakes.
Data-entry and transcription error.

development.question_text: A researcher tests whether a memory supplement improves exam scores. Group 1 receives the supplement and is composed of high-achieving university medical students. Group 2 receives no supplement and is composed of primary school students. Identify the critical fault in this study.
development.solution_text:
The two groups have vastly different baseline cognitive abilities and educational levels before the supplement is administered.
Confounding variable (participant baseline ability).

development.question_text: A survey on household income and personal debt is conducted by a bank loan officer who asks customers direct questions during mortgage interview meetings. Explain why the collected income and debt data may be biased.
development.solution_text:
Applicants may overstate income or conceal informal debts to improve their chances of loan approval with the loan officer.
Interviewer effect and lack of anonymity in a high-stakes setting.

development.question_text: A zoo studies chimpanzee social behaviour by having a researcher in bright clothing stand $1\text{ metre}$ from the enclosure cage taking notes, causing the animals to display agitation. Propose a change to the observation process that removes this fault.
development.solution_text:
The visible presence of the researcher alters natural animal behaviour (observer effect).
Observe the animals via hidden remote cameras or from behind one-way observation glass.

development.question_text: A traffic department studies speeding on a local road by counting only the vehicles stopped by police patrol cars, while vehicles that passed without incident are unrecorded. Identify the fault in this observational record.
development.solution_text:
The dataset contains only offending vehicles and omits all law-abiding drivers, creating an incomplete record.
Missing and incomplete observational records.

mastery.question_text: A pharmaceutical company tests an energy supplement. Participants in the treatment group are given the supplement pill and told it will boost their alertness, while the control group receives nothing and is told they are the untreated control. Both groups then rate their energy levels. Identify two critical faults in this experimental procedure.
mastery.solution_text:
1. Lack of a placebo control (the control group received no pill, so psychological expectations were unequal).
2. Lack of blinding (participants knew their group assignment, inducing confirmation and expectation bias).

mastery.question_text: A university conducts a longitudinal study on student study hours using a single end-of-semester survey where students estimate their daily study time for every week of the 14-week semester. Explain the primary fault and propose an accurate data-collection design.
mastery.solution_text:
Estimating daily study time across 14 past weeks at semester's end causes severe recall error.
Remedy: Replace the retrospective survey with daily digital time-tracking logs or weekly real-time check-ins.

mastery.question_text: A company audits its workplace safety culture. The safety officer interviews workers while the factory supervisor stands alongside them. Workers who report minor safety breaches are asked to sign an acknowledgement form that is placed in their personnel file. Identify two distinct data collection faults in this process and explain how each distorts the results.
mastery.solution_text:
1. Interviewer / authority presence (the supervisor's presence intimidates workers into under-reporting safety breaches for fear of discipline).
2. Lack of confidentiality and anonymity (placing signed reports in personnel files penalises honesty and suppresses reporting of near-misses).
